summary:
### Key Topics Discussed
- Practical checks for address data.
- Handling missing street address information in object metadata.
- Jobs that do not require a street address (e.g., customer garage in a large parking lot).
- Schema for the new delivery register.
- Connection to how selection time is marked.
- Weekly scheduling for tasks.
- System flow for calculating task slot times (e.g., Thursday and Friday, week 29).
- Sorting task lists by type.
- Assigning tasks to specific teams and executors (fine planning).
- Route optimization based on requested/proposed delivery times.
- Adjusting task scheduling in fine planning (drag and drop) if initial route optimization is inefficient.
- Hard versus soft time recommendations for task scheduling.
- Different planning modes in fine planning based on desired delivery times.
- Planner's decision-making in fine planning regarding task order and potential risks.
- Visibility of conflicting information (e.g., parking prohibitions, specific delivery times) within the system.
- Ability to see multiple time slots for tasks.
- Rescheduling jobs to a later week in rough planning if they cannot be completed in the current week.
- Location of the refresh button/filter in the rough planning UI.
- Grouping geographically and time-clustered tasks in rough planning.
- Collapsing multiple tasks within a single stop (e.g., four recycling rooms in one residential area) for faster workflow and creating a grouping function.
- Grouping tasks by address (e.g., Storgatan 22) and execution code.
- System summarization of order value, cost, and production time for each task.
- System automatically grouping multiple tasks of the same type at the same time and address into a "cluster task" with summarized values.

### Decisions Made
- The planner, potentially with the executor, will decide to reorder tasks in fine planning, accepting any associated risks. The system must display information like parking prohibitions or specific delivery times to support this decision.
- Jobs that cannot be completed within the current week's schedule can be moved back to rough planning for scheduling in a subsequent week.
- The refresh button/filter for rough planning will be located in the rough planning UI.

### Important Points & Insights
- The system should look for street address information in the object's metadata. If unavailable, it won't be able to determine the side (right/left) of the street.
- The logic must be able to handle cases where a street address is not relevant or available, such as for a customer garage in a large parking lot.
- The chosen time for a task is not marked directly; instead, tasks are placed on a weekly schedule.
- The system calculates available slot times for tasks based on geographic location and delivery times, which then supports fine planning and task assignment.
- Route optimization is the first step, based on requested delivery times.
- If route optimization indicates inefficiency (e.g., excessive travel), tasks can be moved to different days (e.g., Tuesday) in fine planning using drag and drop.
- The system provides soft recommendations for task scheduling, which can be overridden during fine planning.
- Hard recommendations, such as a food store's opening hours (e.g., not before 9 AM and not after 4 PM), must guide fine planning directly due to strict time windows.
- Fine planning may have different planning modes; the initial mode being planning based on desired or advantageous delivery times for tasks scheduled for the week.
- Fine planning will summarize the travel route, which will be visible on a map, allowing users to identify and understand seemingly illogical routes (e.g., due to parking restrictions or specific time constraints).
- The system needs to provide information such as parking prohibitions or specific desired delivery times to the planner and executor to inform decisions about reordering tasks in fine planning.
- The system should allow users to view multiple available time slots for tasks.
- If a job cannot be completed within the current week (e.g., due to time constraints like not being able to finish before 4 PM on Thursday), it can be returned to rough planning and rescheduled for the following week. This allows the planner to replace it with another job to optimize the current week.
- Grouping tasks that are geographically and time-clustered in rough planning would improve efficiency.
- The UI should support collapsing multiple sub-tasks (e.g., several recycling rooms) into a single logical stop to speed up the workflow.
- The system can group a handful to 20 tasks, for example, 'roll-out bins', at a specific address like Storgatan 22, based on their execution code.
- The system has an existing rough capability to sum up the order value, cost, and production time for each task, in addition to location and time.
- When several tasks of the same type occur at the same time and location, the system will group them into a "cluster task" that summarizes the address, total order value, total production time, and total cost, making it clearer for the planner.

### Open Questions/Pending Items
- How to reduce the number of entities in rough planning (mentioned as a "nice-to-have" function).
